title: Dinosaurs May Have Been Literally Charbroiled After the Asteroid Impact
author: Jake Currie
text: Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisementPaleontologyDinosaurs May Have Been Literally Charbroiled After the Asteroid ImpactA new study reignites the global firestorm debateJCBy Jake Currie9:00 AM CDT on July 29, 2026Add Nautilus to GoogleWe know why the dinosaurs died—a massive asteroid hit the Yucatan Peninsula forming the Chicxulub crater—but how they died is still the subject of debate. To paraphrase Robert Frost, some say it happened with fire, and some say with ice. The “ice” version of events is that a cloud of dust from the impact blotted out the sun enough to cause a drop in global temperatures (similar to a nuclear winter). Subscribe to skip adsFeatured VideoPowered By 102.3K 00OTD in Space – March 26: U.S. Army Launches Explorer 3 SatelliteShareNextStayThe “fire” scenario is much more violent: As material ejected from the impact rained down from the atmosphere, it ignited a global firestorm, essentially cooking almost everything alive. While Team Ice has seemed to have an edge in recent years, Team Fire is coming in hot with a new study published in the Journal of Geophysical Research: Biogeosciences.When the Mt. Everest-sized asteroid responsible for the Chicxulub crater hit, it displaced an enormous plume of vaporized material that spread into the upper atmosphere. It’s the physical characteristics of that plume and immediate aftermath that planetary scientists from Purdue University were focused on modeling in this latest study. Subscribe to skip adsAdvertisement
